-77.37246,35.61322.name: East Carolina University
-77.37246,35.61322.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-80.22500,43.53279.name: University of Guelph
-80.22500,43.53279.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, March 2023
-80.22500,43.53279.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, March 2023. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

12.45696,41.86511.name: Istituto Nationale Malattei Infettive (INMI) Lazzaro Spallanzani
12.45696,41.86511.desc: A BSL4 laboratory, operational. Run by National Institute for Infectious Disease. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in full-body positive-pressure suits with their own air supply. Operational or announced: 2000. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-122.00900,37.54900.name: Synthego
-122.00900,37.54900.desc: Sells synthetic guide RNAs and edited cell lines by catalogue, which is what turned genome editing from a technique into a purchase order. Its position is upstream of everything: a laboratory anywhere with an institutional account can order the exact reagents for a specific edit and have them in days. There is no screening regime covering who may buy them.

16.41600,48.23400.name: Joint FAO/IAEA Centre of Nuclear Techniques in Food and Agriculture
16.41600,48.23400.desc: The programme that funds and coordinates the research behind the sterile insect technique, running projects with fifteen to twenty member states at a time and publishing the results as journal special issues. It set out to build a generic framework for producing male-only strains applicable across pest species, because the classic fruit fly strains depend on mutations that do not transfer. Its stated position on validation is worth recording: any new genetic sexing strain must be tested under mass-rearing conditions and in small-scale pilot trials before deployment in a large programme. That is an intergovernmental body writing a release protocol for engineered insects, outside the Cartagena machinery that governs everything else on this map.
